about.title: Peer Observation Program
about.intro: The Course Peer Observation program for Advanced Computer Programming is designed to enhance teaching quality through a structured, supportive peer review process. This initiative brings together instructors to observe, reflect, and improve their teaching practices in an EMI (English as a Medium of Instruction) context.
objectives: Promote reflective teaching practices among advanced programming educators
Provide constructive, evidence-based feedback on teaching
Share effective teaching strategies for advanced computer programming courses
Enhance EMI teaching skills through peer collaboration
Build a supportive community of practice in advanced programming education

process_steps.title: Pre-Observation Meeting
process_steps.description: Observer and instructor meet to discuss the lesson plan, learning objectives, and specific areas for feedback.

process_steps.title: Classroom Observation
process_steps.description: The observer attends the class session, taking notes on teaching methods, student engagement, and learning activities.

process_steps.title: Post-Observation Discussion
process_steps.description: A reflective discussion where both parties share observations, celebrate strengths, and identify opportunities for improvement.

process_steps.title: Written Feedback
process_steps.description: The observer provides a structured written report summarizing key observations and recommendations.

principles: Confidentiality — Observations are for professional development, not evaluation
Respect — All feedback is delivered constructively and collegially
Reciprocity — Every participant serves as both observer and observed
Growth — The focus is on continuous improvement, not perfection

emi_tdc.title: NSYSU EMI Teaching Development Center
emi_tdc.intro: The EMI Teaching Development Center at National Sun Yat-sen University was established in September 2021 to provide, integrate, and share EMI resources and train university faculty in English-medium instruction. syllabus.title: Syllabus
syllabus.plan_name: From Grinding to Co-Creating: Participatory Learning Action Research in Advanced Programming with LeetCode and CPE

info.department: International Bachelor Program of Computer Science

syllabus.summary: This course addresses the learning challenges students face in advanced programming when preparing for the CPE (Collegiate Programming Examination). It proposes a participatory teaching model using LeetCode as scaffolding. The course uses C/C++ as the primary implementation language, leveraging its high performance and memory management capabilities for exam preparation, supplemented by Python for rapid algorithm logic verification. The plan introduces a participatory learning spirit, breaking the traditional isolated problem-solving approach through Peer Code Review, Pair Programming, and Study Groups to build a collaborative learning community.
syllabus.design_title: Core Framework: Four Principles of Participatory Learning

phases.title: Spiral Thinking Strategy
phases.description: The course follows a spiral cycle: Explore Principles → LeetCode Practice → CPE Challenge → Peer Feedback.

steps.title: Explore
steps.description: Instructor explains core algorithm concepts (e.g., DFS/BFS) with Python demonstrations.

steps.title: Practice
steps.description: Students use C/C++ on LeetCode for basic problems, mastering syntax and edge cases.

steps.title: Challenge
steps.description: Tackle CPE past exam problems with complex I/O and test data.

steps.title: Feedback
steps.description: Group code performance review and deeper optimization in the next cycle.

phases.title: Practical Action Planning
phases.description: The course directly connects to CPE certification and software engineer technical interviews.

steps.title: Mock Exams
steps.description: Conduct in-class CPE simulation exams under real exam time pressure.

steps.title: Daily Challenge
steps.description: Post one daily LeetCode problem via class group to maintain practice.

steps.title: Certification & Career
steps.description: Course output links to CPE scores and personal LeetCode Profile for job applications.

steps.title: Knowledge Base
steps.description: Students build a collaborative CPE solution wiki for future cohorts.

weeks.content: Introduce CPE rules and LeetCode platform. Set up C++ development environment.
CPE-frequent string parsing. Practice stringstream, getline techniques.
Use std::vector, std::list to solve LeetCode array problems.
Use std::map, std::set for frequency statistics (Hash Map applications).
Analyze Big-O of sorting algorithms. Code Review for performance.
LeetCode Binary Search focus. Solve CPE sequence search problems.
Implement GCD, Sieve of Eratosthenes. CPE math problem training.
In-class CPE mock test. Simulate real exam conditions (7 problems / 3 hours).
Classic CPE greedy problems (e.g., scheduling). Group discussion on local optima.
Use Python recursion trees for logic, then implement N-Queens in C++.
From recursion to DP. Introduce Memoization and Tabulation.
Implement LIS, LCS. Essential CPE problem analysis.
Solve maze problems. Implement Queue and Stack for search.
Dijkstra and Floyd-Warshall implementation. Map navigation analysis.
Tree Traversal and Union-Find. Group challenge on hard CPE problems.
Group presentations of CPE solution technical reports with Q&A.

outcomes.title: Knowledge
outcomes.description: Students can explain Big-O time complexity and master 10+ C++ STL containers and their appropriate use cases.

outcomes.title: Skills
outcomes.description: Students can independently solve CPE intermediate problems in C/C++ within 30 minutes with debugging and optimization skills.

outcomes.title: Attitude
outcomes.description: Students shift from fearing programming to enjoying problem-solving challenges and actively participating in tech communities.

deliverables: CPE Solution Handbook: A class-wide collaborative C++ solution codebase compiled as an e-book or GitHub Repo.
LeetCode Portfolio: Each student builds a personal problem-solving profile (solved count, contest scores) for job applications.
Participatory Teaching Module: A complete OBE-integrated participatory learning programming education module.

teaching_methods.title: Teaching Methods
teaching_methods.description: This course centers on participatory learning, combining diverse teaching strategies to break the traditional isolated learning model and enhance outcomes through collaboration and interaction.

methods.title: Scaffolding
methods.subtitle: Learning Scaffolding
methods.description: Using LeetCode as a preliminary scaffold with its user-friendly interface and clear difficulty levels (Easy/Medium/Hard) to guide students progressively into complex CPE problems. The course follows a spiral cycle: Explore Principles → LeetCode Practice → CPE Challenge → Peer Feedback.
points: Explore: Instructor explains core algorithm concepts (e.g., DFS/BFS) with Python demonstrations
Practice: Students switch to C/C++ on LeetCode for basic problems, mastering syntax and edge cases
Challenge: Tackle CPE past exam problems with complex I/O and test data
Feedback: Group code performance review and deeper optimization in the next cycle

methods.title: Jigsaw Classroom
methods.subtitle: Jigsaw Teaching Method
methods.description: Complex algorithm topics are divided into sub-topics, with each student responsible for researching a different sub-topic before returning to their group to teach other members, ensuring every student gains deep understanding and has the opportunity to express themselves.
points: CPE problem types (string processing, sorting, dynamic programming) are assigned to different students for in-depth study
Students become 'experts' on their sub-topic and share problem-solving approaches and C++ implementation techniques with their group
Through peer teaching, students shift from passive listening to active explanation
Develops students' ability to express technical concepts in English, reinforcing EMI learning outcomes

methods.title: Cooperative Learning
methods.subtitle: Collaborative Learning
methods.description: Through mechanisms such as Peer Code Review, Pair Programming, and Problem-Solving Study Groups, a collaborative learning community is established where students construct knowledge through social interaction.
points: Code Review Circles: Weekly group code reviews checking C++ memory usage and runtime efficiency
Pair Programming: Two students work together — one writes code, the other reviews in real-time — building team engineering skills
Problem-Solving Study Groups: Regular discussions of CPE past exam solutions, collaboratively building a solution knowledge base
Student Instructor Mechanism: Students present solutions to specific difficult problems while classmates offer optimization suggestions

methods.title: Engaged Learning
methods.subtitle: Participatory Learning
methods.description: Student-centered learning driven by real-world problem domains (CPE certification, technical interviews), combining daily challenges and mock exams to encourage active participation and deep engagement.
points: Mock Exams: In-class CPE simulation tests replicating real exam time pressure and conditions
Daily Challenge: One daily LeetCode problem posted via class group to maintain practice momentum
Learning Portfolio: Each student builds a personal LeetCode Profile tracking solved count and acceptance rate
Reflective Journal: Students record weekly difficulties and breakthroughs to promote metacognitive development

feedback.title: Observation Feedback
feedback.description: After the observation, please fill out the Classroom Observation Form to help the instructor continuously improve their teaching. All feedback is confidential and used solely for professional development.
instructions: Download the Classroom Observation Form below.
Based on the items in the form, provide specific observations and suggestions regarding teaching content, methods, and student engagement.
Once completed, please send the form to the instructor or course coordinator.
